title: DROP VIEW
description: Learn how to remove views from the database using the DROP VIEW statement.

data.text: To remove a view from a database, use the DROP VIEW statement. The IF EXISTS clause prevents an error when dropping a view that does not exist.

data.title: DROP VIEW with IF EXISTS
data.content: Safely drops a view if it exists.

data.title: Drop the daily_sales view
data.content: Removes the daily_sales view from the database.

data.title: Drop multiple views at once
data.content: Removes multiple views in a single statement.

data.text: Note that when you drop a view, SQL Server removes all permissions associated with the view.

data.title: DROP VIEW Key Points
points: Use DROP VIEW to remove views from the database.
Always use IF EXISTS to avoid errors on non-existent views.
Dropping a view removes all permissions on that view.
You can drop multiple views in a single DROP VIEW statement.
